flagged.title: Meena's World & Tollington
flagged.reason: The video presents two fabricated quotations ('I do not have a name for what I felt' as the novel's opening line, and 'I'm not lying, I'm just telling a story') as key direct textual quotations for students to analyse and memorise.

mark_affecting.quote: Meera Syal uses this incredibly powerful opening line as the emotional engine for the whole book. Meena says: 'I do not have a name for what I felt.'
when she gets called out on it, she insists: 'I'm not lying, I'm just telling a story.'

flagged.title: The Ending & Growing Up
flagged.reason: The video instructs students to memorize and quote two fabricated lines ('If you can't fit in, you might as well stand out' and 'This is also my home') that do not appear in the novel.

mark_affecting.quote: Now you should absolutely write this down and memorize it for your exams: 'If you can't fit in, you might as well stand out.' This single powerful line basically represents the novel's true emotional resolution
Right near the end, Meena reflects, 'This is also my home.' This incredibly simple statement is the ultimate synthesis of her identity.

flagged.title: Narrative Voice & Structure
flagged.reason: The video invents and displays a fake quotation ('I do not have a name for what I felt.') as the opening line of the novel, which directly contradicts the lesson text and would lead students to cite an incorrect quotation in an exam.

mark_affecting.video_says: Take a look at this opening line. 'I do not have a name for what I felt.' ... deliberately chose these exact words and placed them right at the start of the book
mark_affecting.lesson_says: The opening line demonstrates this dual perspective immediately: 'I do not have many memories of my very early childhood, apart from the obvious ones, of course.'

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: F1 is mark-affecting because the video instructs students to prepare for a two-part exam with a separate 'Wider Text Essay' assessed on AO4 context, when Eduqas has a single 40-mark source-based question where context is not assessed.

mark_affecting.quote: Two-Part Question... Part 4: Wider Text Essay - Themes & AO4 Context... tackling the wider text, where we synthesise those themes with your AO4 context.
